outcome: Rate of patients requesting cesarean section during labor
cohort: The study included 225 pregnant women from Turkey, divided into an intervention group (75 patients attending pregnancy school after the 14th week of pregnancy) and a control group (150 patients who did not attend pregnancy school).
finding: Antenatal education positively impacted women's birth beliefs, shifting the perception of childbirth from a medical intervention to a natural process, and was associated with a lower rate of requested cesarean sections and labor arrest.
mod_finding: The control group, who did not attend pregnancy school, had a significantly higher rate of requesting cesarean section during labor (73.4% vs 47.2%) and a higher rate of labor arrest leading to cesarean section (26.6% vs 8.3%).
